name: Passage de la Brocante · Flea-Market Passage

st_brocante.name: Allée du Partage · Sharing Alley
st_brocante.alt: A rainy autumn afternoon seen down the length of a long stone flea-market arcade, rain pouring past the arches and townsfolk hurrying by under umbrellas: in front a mime kneels to fill a big wicker basket to overflowing with hair combs; by the stall an old stallholder and a mime haggle over a brass gramophone; far back a mime stands on an upturned crate holding open a blank scroll; a mime hands red apples to two small children under a red umbrella; a green-beret mime shares out paper party hats to the children. The stone archway on the far left leads back to the market square; the orange, teal and plum doors along the arcade wall lead on.

doors.label: Rue de la Monnaie · Coin Street

entrepots.name: Quai des Entrepôts · Warehouse Quay
entrepots.alt: An autumn riverside warehouse quay behind the flea market: a mime carries an old armchair into the warehouse, striking a pose; one holds a big blue vase, peeling off its mark; one hands a loaf of bread to each of the small children; one with a miner's headlamp over his beret digs into a heap of coal; one balances a tall stack of teacups on one hand, standing on one foot. The orange door on the left leads back to the alley.

monnaie.name: Rue de la Monnaie · Coin Street
monnaie.alt: An autumn street of curiosity stalls under big cumulus clouds: a mime drops coins into the hatch of a yellow toy submarine; one pours colored liquid out of old bottles at a clearance stall; one blows a brass trumpet that sprays out gold coins; one wears three hats stacked on his beret; one sits in a red pedal-car taxi holding out a tin for a coin. The teal door on the left leads back to the alley.

surcharges.name: Impasse des Surcharges · Overload Court
surcharges.alt: A cozy autumn courtyard at the back of the flea market, with a tea stall and a dressmaker's mannequin: a mime pushes a hand-cart piled sky-high with chairs, lamps and suitcases; one cranks an old lantern until it glows; one plants a sapling in a big silver racing trophy cup; one pays the tea lady with a coin and a brass key; one lifts a golden crown off the mannequin. The plum door on the left leads back to the alley.
